text:
maria: Quick sync  re: making charts more compact on dashboards. thinking: truncate axis label to one line, add a small unit pill next to the axis title, and reduce legend to 2 lines. any major concerns? :thinking_face:

jake: mock please? want to see how long legend names flow around the pill. also how does it look on mobile narrow widths.

maria: Figma: https://figma.com/file/xxx/compact-chart-proto and screenshot attached.

olivia: unit pill looks neat, but when we abbreviate units (K/M/B) the pill alone can be ambiguous. i suggest pill has a full-text hover ("thousands", "millions") and the aria label reads the expanded text.

samir: strong +1. also: smoothing control placement. currently it's in the toolbar header; feels disconnected from series selection. could we add a tiny inline toggle inside the legend when there is only a single series selected?

maria: proposal: legend max lines = 2, axis.labelMaxLines = 1, unitPill = true (right-aligned). smoothing move to chart toolbar but change DOM order so legend items tab first then smoothing. snippet used in prototype (for reference, not parsed):
```json
{ "yAxis": { "labelMaxLines": 1, "unitPill": true, "unitMode": "auto" }, "legend": { "maxLines": 2, "compact": true }, "toolbar": { "items": ["legendMenu","export","smoothingToggle"] } }
```

jake: accessibility note: unit pill should have aria-label like "Units: millions" and not rely on visual spacing. also the pill needs contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 when used as background.

olivia: keyboard order: ensure smoothing toggle is focusable immediately after legend entries. currently our toolbar renders after the canvas which breaks linear reading order. we should move toolbar markup to be before the canvas in DOM for keyboard users, but visually keep it above.

samir: outlier handling: current autoscale hides smaller variations when a single spike appears. two options: 1) cap mode (compress values above a threshold and show a marker for capped points), 2) annotate outliers with a dot + tooltip and preserve scale. prefer #2 by default, but allow cap mode as user pref.

jake: microcopy suggestion for tooltip: "Outlier: 12.3M. Turn on 'cap max' to compress axes." shorter alternative: "Outlier: 12.3M  cap to compress."

olivia: a11y for outliers: do not rely on color only. use a patterned stroke or small icon and include descriptive text in tooltip that screenreaders announce. Also ensure the outlier marker has a 12px target for keyboard focus.

maria: items to action: 1) add aria-label + hover expand for unit pill; 2) ensure pill copy variants (e.g., "Units: USD" vs "USD") in prototype for testing; 3) move smoothing toggle into toolbar and fix tab order; 4) add outlier marker + tooltip + optional cap mode; 5) include keyboard/a11y tests in QA checklist.

designbot: created issue #2468: "compact axis + unit pill + outlier markers" assigned to @maria and @samir.

samir: i'll mock the outlier marker tomorrow and include both cap and annotate flows. will flag for quick UX pass. :thumbsup:

jake: one more microcopy nit: prefer explicit "Units: USD" when axis could be ambiguous (e.g., daily active users vs dollars).

maria: noted  i'll add both copy options to the prototype and we can A/B. updating figma and will ping when ready.

olivia: tiny follow-up: ensure exported PNGs include the unit pill text. docs rely on screenshot clarity.

maria: added to checklist. closing when prototypes are uploaded. :sparkles:
